title: Graphs II: Shortest Paths (0-1 BFS, State/Implicit Dijkstra, Multi-source, k-shortest)
relevance: High — grid/maze races, one coupon / one free edge, multi-source infection, and state-augmented shortest paths dominate mid OA + Div2 C/D; stretch covers k-shortest and potentials mindset toward CM.
company_notes: One free upgrade / coupon: cheapest route if you may halve or zero exactly one edge — Flight Discount clones in delivery/ride-share OAs. Infection / facility placement: multi-source BFS/Dijkstra from all hospitals, Wi-Fi routers, or ACs; answer min time or best spot (Air Conditioners / Christmas Trees). State-augmented travel: pick up one bike / key / discount → dist[u][have] Dijkstra (Bicycles / elevator-vs-stairs). Maze with asymmetric moves: limited left/right presses or teleporters — 0-1 BFS / hub nodes rather than plain BFS (Labyrinth / Third Avenue).

phases.goal: Establish that the candidate maps the prompt to 0-1 edges, implicit/state graphs, multi-source, coupon, or k-shortest rather than named Dijkstra.

must_hit.point: Contest shortest-path prompts rarely say run Dijkstra; edges are often 0/1, the graph is implicit (grid, residues, portals), or the vertex is a state (node, resource).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names 0/1 edges, implicit grid/residues/portals, or state (node, resource) as the modeling cue.

must_hit.point: Multi-source means seed every source at dist 0, or reverse the graph and start from all sinks.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says enqueue all sources at 0 or reverse edges and BFS/Dijkstra from all sinks.

must_hit.point: One coupon / one free edge is state Dijkstra (layer) or the two-Dijkstra coupon trick on every edge.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps halve/zero exactly one edge to a coupon layer or fwd+bwd try-on-every-edge.

must_hit.point: k-shortest keeps the first k pops per node; Potentials/Johnson is for many SSSP queries when negatives may exist but there is no neg-cycle.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions ≤k pops per node and/or Bellman-Ford potentials then Dijkstra APSP.

probes: Does this look like 0-1 BFS, state Dijkstra, multi-source, a coupon trick, or k-shortest—and what wording tipped you off?

hints.1: Ask whether edge weights are only two values, whether the vertex needs extra state, and how many sources start at once.
hints.2: 0/1 → deque 0-1 BFS; (node, resource) → state SP; many starts → multi-source; one special edge → coupon; first k arrivals → k-shortest.
hints.3: Say: rarely named Dijkstra; 0/1, implicit, or state (node, resource); multi-source seeds all at dist 0 (or reverse from sinks); coupon = layer or two Dijkstras; k-shortest = first k pops; Johnson when many SSSP with possible negatives and no neg-cycle.

phases.goal: Choose 0-1 BFS, state Dijkstra, multi-source seeding, the coupon two-Dijkstra pattern, or k-shortest pops before coding.

must_hit.point: 0-1 BFS uses a deque: push_front on weight 0, push_back on weight 1.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States deque with front for 0-cost and back for 1-cost edges.

must_hit.point: State Dijkstra stores dist[node][extra…] (or a hashed state) and relaxes transitions, not only original edges.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names dist indexed by node plus coupon/bike/dir/streak and transitions on that state.

must_hit.point: Multi-source: initialize the queue/PQ with all sources at 0; reverse edges when asking nearest source to each node.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Seeds every source at 0 and mentions reversing for nearest-source queries.

must_hit.point: Two-Dijkstra coupon: fwd from s, bwd from t on the reversed graph; try the special op on every edge (e.g. fwd[u]+floor(w/2)+bwd[v]).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes fwd/bwd pair and evaluating the discount on each edge.

must_hit.point: k-shortest: keep ≤k distances per node; the i-th pop is the i-th best under nonnegative weights.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Allows up to k pops/distances per node and prints k costs.

probes: Walk through which algorithm you pick and how you initialize distances for this prompt.
For a one-coupon route, do you use a state layer or the two-Dijkstra try-every-edge trick?

hints.1: Separate weight pattern (0/1 vs general), state extras, and how many sources you seed.
hints.2: 0/1 → deque front/back; extra resource → dist[node][extra]; all starts at 0 or reverse; coupon → fwd/bwd or layer; k → ≤k pops.
hints.3: Say: deque push_front(0)/push_back(1); state Dijkstra on transitions; multi-source all at 0 (reverse for nearest); fwd from s + bwd from t + special op per edge; ≤k distances / i-th pop is i-th best.

phases.goal: Verify deque pushes, Dijkstra stale-entry skip, path aggregates on relax, and hub/portal modeling details.

must_hit.point: Implement 0-1 BFS with a deque: push_front on weight 0, push_back on weight 1.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Codes or narrates front/back pushes keyed by edge weight 0 vs 1.

must_hit.point: Dijkstra hygiene: if (d > dist[u]) continue; before relaxing (USACO Guide TLE trap).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Skips outdated PQ entries before neighbor relaxations.

must_hit.point: Path aggregates on the shortest DAG: while running Dijkstra, update count / min-edges / max-edges on == and < relaxations.
must_hit.evidence_hint: On strict improvement resets aggregates; on equal distance updates count or min/max edges.

must_hit.point: Grid portals: use virtual letter/hub nodes with 0/1 edges instead of a naïve teleport clique.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Attaches cells to hub nodes rather than connecting every portal pair.

probes: Show the 0-1 BFS enqueue rule and where you put the Dijkstra d > dist[u] continue.
How do you update path count or min/max edges when a relaxation ties versus improves?

hints.1: Check the deque push side and whether stale PQ distances still relax.
hints.2: Weight 0 → front, weight 1 → back; skip if d > dist[u]; on < reset aggregates, on == merge counts/min/max; portals via hubs.
hints.3: Say: push_front(0)/push_back(1); if (d > dist[u]) continue before relax; ==/< update count and min/max edges; virtual letter hubs with 0/1 edges beat a teleport clique.

phases.goal: State 0-1 BFS linear cost and when Johnson needs Bellman-Ford plus n Dijkstras.

must_hit.point: Potentials / Johnson: Bellman-Ford from a super-source gives potentials p[v]; reweight w'(u,v)=w(u,v)+p[u]-p[v] ≥ 0; then n Dijkstras for APSP; restore dist = dist' - p[u] + p[v].
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sketches BF potentials, nonnegative reweight, n Dijkstras, and dist restore.

probes: What is the time for 0-1 BFS, and when do you reach for Johnson instead of one Dijkstra?
After reweighting with potentials, how do you recover original distances?

hints.1: Compare linear 0-1 BFS to needing many SSSP on a graph that may have negatives.
hints.2: 0-1 BFS is O(V+E); Johnson = BF potentials, reweight ≥ 0, then n Dijkstras, then restore.
hints.3: Say: 0-1 BFS O(V+E); BF super-source → p[v]; w'=w+p[u]-p[v] ≥ 0; n Dijkstras; dist = dist' - p[u] + p[v].

phases.goal: Catch stale Dijkstra entries, single-source seeding, clique teleports, and relaxing only original edges.

must_hit.point: Omitting if (d > dist[u]) continue; before relaxing is the USACO Guide Dijkstra TLE trap.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names skipping outdated PQ pops as required hygiene.

must_hit.point: Seeding only one source instead of all sources at dist 0 breaks multi-source shortest paths.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Insists every source starts in the queue/PQ at 0.

must_hit.point: Building a naïve teleport clique instead of virtual hub nodes with 0/1 edges blows the model.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Prefers letter/hub nodes over all-pairs portal edges.

must_hit.point: State Dijkstra must relax transitions on dist[node][extra…], not only the original graph edges.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says neighbors are state transitions (coupon/bike/dir), not just raw edges.

probes: What goes wrong if you skip the Dijkstra stale-distance continue, or seed only one multi-source start?
Why are portal hubs safer than connecting every teleport pair?

hints.1: Check PQ skip, how many sources you enqueue, and whether portals densify the graph.
hints.2: Stale d > dist[u] → TLE; multi-source needs all at 0; hubs not cliques; relax state transitions.
hints.3: Say: always if (d > dist[u]) continue; seed every source at dist 0; virtual hubs with 0/1 edges; state Dijkstra relaxes dist[node][extra…] transitions.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: When every edge weight is 0 or 1, use a deque (push_front on 0, push_back on 1) for O(V+E); use Dijkstra when weights are general nonnegative.
Layer/state Dijkstra tracks whether the coupon is used in dist[node][have]; the two-Dijkstra trick runs fwd from s and bwd from t on the reversed graph and tries the special op on every edge.

tradeoffs.topic: Portal hubs vs naïve teleport clique
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Attach cells to virtual letter/hub nodes with 0/1 edges instead of connecting all portal pairs into a dense clique.
Seed every source at dist 0 for simultaneous starts; reverse edges and start from all sinks when the ask is nearest source to each node.
For many SSSP queries on a graph that may have negatives but no neg-cycle: Bellman-Ford potentials, reweight to nonnegative, run n Dijkstras, restore distances.

gotchas.trap: Running Dijkstra without if (d > dist[u]) continue; before relaxing.
gotchas.correction: Skip outdated PQ entries before neighbor relaxations — the USACO Guide TLE trap.

gotchas.trap: Starting multi-source BFS/Dijkstra from a single source.
gotchas.correction: Initialize the queue/PQ with all sources at dist 0 (or reverse and start from all sinks).

gotchas.trap: Using plain BFS on a maze with asymmetric 0/1 move costs.
gotchas.correction: Use 0-1 BFS: deque, push_front on weight 0, push_back on weight 1.
Add virtual letter/hub nodes with 0/1 edges (Third Avenue style).

gotchas.trap: Relaxing only original edges when the vertex is a state (coupon, best bike, direction streak).
gotchas.correction: Store dist[node][extra…] and relax state transitions.

gotchas.trap: Keeping only one distance per node for k-shortest paths.
gotchas.correction: Keep ≤k distances per node; the i-th pop is the i-th best under nonnegative weights.
